title: Area of Composite Figures
seo_title: Grade 7 Area of Composite Figures Worksheets (TEKS 7.9C, STAAR)
standard_text: 7.9C determine the area of composite figures containing combinations of rectangles, squares, parallelograms, trapezoids, triangles, semicircles, and quarter circles
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 worksheets for Texas TEKS 7.9C: area of composite figures with rectangles, triangles, trapezoids, semicircles and quarter circles, cut-out shapes and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Split into known shapes; add the parts and subtract the holes.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Split a composite figure into shapes you know: rectangles, triangles, trapezoids, semicircles and quarter circles.
  • Find each area, then add. If a part is cut out, subtract it.
  • A semicircle is ½ of πr²; a quarter circle is ¼ of πr².
  • Check that every length you use matches the shape it belongs to.

Examples

Example

8 m × 6 m rectangle with a semicircle on the 6 m side

48 + ½ × 3.14 × 3²

48 + 14.13

Answer: 62.13 m²

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the whole circleA semicircle is half: ½ × πr².
Using the diameter as the radiusr = d ÷ 2.
Adding a cut-out partSubtract the part that is removed.
